content:
incident-bot: INCIDENT CREATED 1781234567 - cluster=inference-prod: detected node flapping (NotReady / kubelet restarts) on gpu-node-3,gpu-node-7. PagerDuty notified to #eng-oncall.

Maya S: I'm on call — seeing spike in 5xxs for /v1/generate from inference-pool-prod. Alerts started ~3m ago. Paging infra.

Kevin L: digging in now, pulling node events.

Kevin L: `kubectl get nodes` ->
```
gpu-node-1   Ready    12d

gpu-node-3   NotReady 2m

gpu-node-5   Ready    8d

gpu-node-7   NotReady 1m
```

Kevin L: `kubectl describe node gpu-node-3` shows kubelet restarted 3x in last 5m; Last heartbeat lost. Kernel messages include OOM killers.

Dina R: also seeing inference-runtime pods in inference-prod crashlooping. Pod logs show `RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory` and occasional `failed to allocate memory on device`.

Samir C: is that a driver/host-level OOM or the model exhausting GPU mem? Could be a leak.

Kevin L: collected syslog: ``
[ 1234.567890] Out of memory: Kill process 2345 (python) total-vm: ...
[ 1234.568000] oom_reaper: reaped process 2345
``
Kubelet logs: `syncLoop (housekeeping) failed: rpc error: code = Unknown desc = containerd: container not found` — intermittent.

ops-bot: Notifying infra-oncall and posting to #incidents.

Maya S: immediate mitigation: cordon gpu-node-3,gpu-node-7 and start drains. We'll route traffic off this inference pool to fallback pools. Samir — can you apply a routing policy now?

Samir C: applied routing change: inference-pool-prod -> cpu-quantized-fallback (70%) + remaining gpu nodes (30%). Enabled canary for heavy requests. Keep an eye on latency and quality metrics.

Kevin L: starting drain: `kubectl drain gpu-node-3 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` — some pods are stuck (local PVs).

Dina R: for stuck pods I'm deleting the serving container pods to force reschedule: `kubectl delete pod inference-runtime-xyz -n inference-prod` — they come back on other nodes.

Kevin L: I restarted kubelet on gpu-node-3 (`systemctl restart kubelet`). It came back then flapped again 1m later. Suspecting kernel-level OOM under heavy model load.

Samir C: cluster-autoscaler spun up 2 new gpu nodes in pool-prod (ETA ~4m). Monitoring provisioning.

Maya S: customer impact: 3 customers reported elevated latency, 1 reported 502s. Not a global outage but degraded for heavy throughput jobs. Affected customers: C-8893, C-1120, C-3412. Support team notified.

Kevin L: plan: continue draining problem nodes, collect dmesg + nvml logs, and if flapping continues we'll evict largest pods (lower priority) and schedule heavy jobs on fresh nodes. Also check recent driver rollout.

infra-oncall: looking at host-level telemetry — correlates with recent nvidia-driver 525.x rollout on these nodes. We're preparing a rollback to 515 on a small set to validate.

Dina R: short workaround: add nodeSelector to force heavy-model pods onto nodes with driver 515 or use affinity to avoid flapping hosts. Preparing patch for scheduler.

Samir C: routing update: moved 90% of SLA-bound traffic to dedicated-reserved pool so customers with SLAs have minimal impact. Graceful fallback enabled for others.

Maya S: on-call handoff: I'll keep incident doc updated. Kevin will stay as primary for the next 40m. Samir/Dina will own routing and pod reschedules. I'll inform commercial/support to message affected customers and track replies.

PagerDuty: Acknowledged by Kevin L.

Kevin L: posting initial incident notes to /incidents/1781234567 and will start a postmortem draft once stabilized. Observables to capture: kernel OOM patterns, driver version, per-pod GPU memory trends, kubelet restart timestamps, and any correlation with batch jobs.

Maya S: thanks all — great triage. Adding reactions :eyes: :thumbsup:. If nodes stay stable for 30m we can mark paging resolved, otherwise will escalate to platform-sev.

Maya S: (closing note) paging quiet at 1781234860 — continued monitoring; will update channel with follow-ups and postmortem link when available.
